title: Automated tenant ejection and reservation recalibration postmortem and action plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: During a dedicated-cluster capacity event on 2025-02-17 a single tenant's bursty traffic pattern caused sustained reservation exhaustion and a cascading eviction/latency spike across colocated workloads. The immediate impact was elevated tail latency for medium- and high-priority tenants and ~45 minutes of degraded throughput for affected Dedicated customers.

Root cause: three factors combined:
1) Anomalous tenant workload: a sudden increase in long-context streaming requests from a single tenant with poor retry/backoff.
2) Reservation sizing gap: heuristics for initial reservation and decay were tuned for steady-state throughput and under-provisioned for high-variance tenants.
3) Burst policy configuration: the token-bucket burst curve permitted multi-minute sustained bursts before enforced throttling, allowing a runaway KV-cache growth and allocator pressure that triggered eviction sweeps.

Immediate mitigations performed during incident:
- Applied temporary soft-ejection rule to the offending tenant (throttle to 10% of usual QPS) to stop the runaway.
- Manually increased reservation for impacted nodes to reduce cross-tenant contention.
- Enabled emergency eviction-cooldown to avoid oscillating allocator behavior.

Action items (scope, owner, ETA):
1) Automated soft-isolation playbook (owner: Marcus Chen, ETA: 2025-03-12) - Implement a verified, auditable workflow that automatically applies a graduated isolation policy when per-tenant resource anomalies are detected (detect -> warn -> soft-throttle -> hard-throttle -> notify SRE/PM). Must include manual override and audit log.
2) Reservation recomputation service (owner: Priya Rao, ETA: 2025-03-20) - Build a background service that periodically recomputes per-tenant reservation baselines using percentiles (P50/P95) and burst variance knobs; expose a dry-run mode and reconciliation dashboard.
3) Burst policy rework and step-down curve (owner: Linh Tran, ETA: 2025-03-10) - Replace current single-token-bucket with multi-tiered curve: short spikes allowed, sustained multi-minute bursts trigger exponential backoff. Add unit tests and canary on a non-prod pool.
4) Telemetry & alerting expansion (owner: Marcus Chen, ETA: 2025-03-04) - New signals: reservation_exhaustion_seconds, tenant_kv_cache_growth_rate, sustained_burst_minutes. Tie to a PagerDuty rule when thresholds exceeded.
5) Chaos/resilience tests for allocator (owner: SRE team, ETA: 2025-04-01) - Add deterministic fuzz tests that simulate high-variance tenants and verify eviction/allocator stability.
6) Postmortem playbook & runbook update (owner: Aisha Patel, ETA: 2025-03-06) - Document steps, runbooks, and playbook flows; add checklist for PM/SE incident comms.

Acceptance criteria:
- Automated soft-isolation fires in response to a synthetic tenant that exceeds P99-reservation for >2 minutes in staging and can be disabled manually.
- Reservation recomputation exposes dashboard with historical baselines and a reconciliation job that can be run on demand.
- Burst policy unit tests cover 0-30s, 30s-3min, >3min cases and are included in the runtime CI gate.
- New alerts produce actionable incidents with <5% false positives in a 2-week evaluation window.

Longer-term recommendations (post-release):
- Explore per-tenant ML anomaly detection for traffic shape rather than simple rate rules.
- Consider per-tenant soft cgroup-style resource limits to reduce eviction blast radius.
- Evaluate whether tenant admission controls for Dedicated pools are warranted for very high variance customers.

Notes on trade-offs: Automated isolation reduces blast radius but carries a false-positive risk that can impact legitimate spikes; the design here favors a graduated approach with human-in-the-loop escalation for the first rollout. Reservation recomputation favors stability over aggressive shrinkage to avoid repeat oscillations.
